Priya Raman: Hey — quick question about PR workflow for someone landing their first change in the runtime repo. Branch naming, who to ping for reviews, labels, CI expectations? I skimmed CONTRIBUTING but it's a bit scattered.

Devon Li: Welcome! Short version: follow CODEOWNERS for reviewers, use the branch/tag/label conventions below, and keep PRs small. Longer version: see below.

Priya Raman: Awesome — can you spell out the branch/PR naming?

Kai Nguyen: We usually do: feature/<initials>-<short-desc> for new features, fix/<initials>-<ticket> for bug fixes, chore/<initials>-<desc> for maintenance. Example: feature/pr-ttl-cache-opt or fix/pn-5126-kv-ttl. Try to keep the short-desc <= 5 words.

Mira Chen: Also add the JIRA/ticket id in the PR description header if there's one. Helps backporting.

Priya Raman: Got it. Any size limits?

Devon Li: Prefer <300 lines changed for reviews. If larger, mark as WIP/draft and include a clear PR checklist and testing plan. Small UX tweaks and docs can be smaller (<50 LOC).

Priya Raman: How should I run the tests and lint locally? I hit a flaky test earlier.

Kai Nguyen: Run unit tests: `./scripts/run_tests.sh --fast` or `make test`. Lint: `npm run lint` or `./scripts/lint`. For integration smoke: `./scripts/integration_smoke.sh`. If CI flakes, rerun the failing job from the GitHub UI and ping #eng-oncall if it keeps failing.

jen-ci-bot: CI: build/1234 (runtime) failed on matrix node 2 — timeout on integration test 'kv-cache-flaky'. Re-run with `gh workflow run re-run` or use the rerun button.

Priya Raman: If CI keeps failing after rerun, do we revert?

Devon Li: Don't revert unless the main branch is red AND the change caused it. Instead: mark the PR `needs-investigation`, add @kai or @mira depending on area, and open a follow-up ticket. We avoid emergency reverts unless it's a prod incident.

Priya Raman: How do reviewers get added? Is it automatic?

Mira Chen: CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers for files they own. For cross-cutting changes, add `@team-runtime` (use the GitHub team handle) or directly @mention people in the PR body. Also add the label `needs-review`.

Devon Li: Labels we use: `needs-review`, `size/XS|S|M|L`, `backport-needed` (if applicable), `docs`, `infra`. Use `size/*` so reviewers know expected effort.

Priya Raman: Where's CODEOWNERS & contributing canonical doc?

Kai Nguyen: It's at `.github/CODEOWNERS` and `.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`. The runtime-specific guide is in `docs/runtime/PR_GUIDELINES.md` (search repo root docs/).

Priya Raman: Thanks — last q: draft PR vs normal PR?

Devon Li: Draft PRs for in-progress work or when you want early feedback. Convert to regular PR when ready for review. Always add a checklist: linker tests, perf notes, compat matrix if touching inference runtime.

Priya Raman: Perfect — I'll open a small draft first and ping @Kai for a quick look.

Kai Nguyen: Sounds good. Ping me with the PR link. :thumbsup:

Mira Chen: Also FYI — we tag docs reviewers separately with `docs` label if you changed any READMEs.

Priya Raman: Opening draft now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3420 (draft) — thanks!
